since_last_discussion.speaker: game_master
since_last_discussion.text:
Here's the vote result for day 4:
  player_1 voted to eliminate player_5
  player_3 voted to eliminate player_5
  player_5 voted to eliminate player_3
  player_6 voted to eliminate player_5
  player_8 voted to eliminate player_5
  player_9 voted to eliminate player_5
Player player_5 has been voted out and was a trailseer.
The record of player_5, the trailseer: night 1, followed player_1; they visited no one; night 2, was roleblocked; night 3, was roleblocked.

since_last_discussion.speaker: game_master
since_last_discussion.text: Night of day 4: player_6 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a healer. The record of player_6, the healer: night 1, protected player_8; no attack on them was announced; night 2, protected player_3; no attack on them was announced; night 3, protected player_3, who was attacked and saved.

earlier_today.speaker: player_1
earlier_today.text: Player 3's sigil caught the chanteuse, so player 3 is our confirmed sigilist. That leaves player 8 and player 9 as the remaining pool for the wolves or the necromancer.

earlier_today.speaker: player_3
earlier_today.text: Player 1 makes a fair point about narrowing things down to player 8 and player 9. Let's look closely at how the votes split on day 4 when player 5 was eliminated to see who pushed hardest there and who might be hiding.

earlier_today.speaker: player_8
earlier_today.text: If we are checking the day 4 votes on player 5, player 9 was right there on that lynch too. We need to look closely at who initiated that push rather than assuming everyone not claiming a PR is automatically guilty.

earlier_today.speaker: player_9
earlier_today.text: Everyone piled onto player 5 yesterday once the trailseer claim looked shaky, so pointing at my vote there doesn't single me out. If we want to find where the remaining threats are, we should examine who is pushing narratives instead of circling back to a unified town vote.

earlier_today.speaker: player_8
earlier_today.text: It is true most people ended up on player 5, but player 9 is actively dodging when we try to analyze who started that push. Dismissing voting patterns entirely just helps the remaining threats blend in.
